text: # MediCore University Academic Regulations 2026

## [ATT-1.1] Purpose of Attendance Regulations

Attendance requirements are established to ensure that students participate
regularly in academic activities and remain engaged with their registered
courses. Attendance is recorded for lectures, tutorials, laboratory sessions,
seminars and other compulsory academic activities.

## [ATT-1.2] General Attendance Requirement

Every student enrolled in an undergraduate programme must maintain a minimum
attendance of 75% in each registered course during the semester.

Students whose attendance falls below the prescribed minimum may be declared
ineligible to appear for the corresponding end-semester examination.

Attendance is calculated using the total number of scheduled academic sessions
conducted during the semester.

## [ATT-1.3] Attendance Recording

Faculty members are responsible for recording attendance accurately for every
scheduled academic session.

Students are expected to verify their attendance records periodically through
the university's academic portal.

Any discrepancy in an attendance record must be reported to the concerned
faculty member within seven calendar days of the record being published.

## [ATT-1.4] Shortage of Attendance

A student whose attendance is below the required percentage shall normally be
required to compensate for the shortage through officially approved academic
activities where such activities are available.

Participation in optional events, student clubs, cultural activities or
informal study sessions does not automatically count toward course attendance.

## [ATT-1.5] Attendance and Examination Eligibility

Attendance eligibility is assessed before the commencement of the end-semester
examination period.

A student who does not satisfy the minimum attendance requirement may be
prevented from appearing for the examination in the affected course.

## [EXAM-2.1] Semester Examinations

End-semester examinations are conducted according to the academic calendar
published by the university.

Students must complete the examination registration process within the
prescribed period.

## [EXAM-2.2] Examination Registration

Only students who have completed examination registration and satisfy all
academic eligibility requirements may normally appear for an examination.

The examination office may withhold an examination admit card where a student
has outstanding administrative requirements.

## [EXAM-2.3] Examination Conduct

Students must arrive at the examination venue before the reporting time
specified on the examination schedule.

Students must carry their university identification card and examination
admit card unless an alternative arrangement has been formally communicated.

## [EXAM-2.4] Permitted Materials

Only materials specifically authorized by the examination office may be taken
into an examination room.

Electronic devices may not be used during an examination unless the
examination instructions explicitly authorize their use.

## [EXAM-2.5] Absence from Examination

A student who does not attend a scheduled examination will ordinarily be
recorded as absent.

Requests for consideration of examination absence must be submitted through
the procedure prescribed by the examination office.

## [EXAM-2.6] Medical Examination Absence

A student who is unable to attend an examination because of a documented
medical emergency may submit a medical request for consideration.

The request must be supported by documentation from a recognized medical
practitioner and submitted within the period specified by the examination
office.

Approval of a medical request does not automatically guarantee a replacement
examination.

## [MED-3.1] Medical Attendance Consideration

Students experiencing significant medical circumstances during a semester may
apply for attendance consideration.

The application must include appropriate medical documentation and must be
submitted through the designated academic office.

## [MED-3.2] Medical Attendance Relaxation

Where a student's medical circumstances are formally verified, the Academic
Review Committee may consider attendance relaxation.

A medically verified student may be considered eligible for an examination
with attendance as low as 65%, provided that the required medical documents
have been approved.

## [MED-3.3] Medical Documentation

Medical documents must clearly identify the period during which the student
was unable to participate in normal academic activities.

The university may request additional documentation where the submitted
material is insufficient to establish the circumstances described in the
application.

## [MED-3.4] Committee Review

Medical attendance requests are reviewed individually.

The committee may approve, partially approve or reject an application after
considering the submitted documentation and academic circumstances.

## [FEE-4.1] Semester Fees

Students must pay applicable semester fees within the payment period
announced by the university.

The applicable fee schedule is published through official university
communication channels.

## [FEE-4.2] Fee Payment Deadline

The standard deadline for payment of semester fees is the date specified in
the official fee schedule.

Students are responsible for checking the published schedule and completing
payment before the deadline.

## [FEE-4.3] Late Payment

A student who fails to pay fees by the standard deadline may be required to pay
a late payment charge.

Late payment may be accepted only during an officially announced late-payment
period.

## [FEE-4.4] Outstanding Fees

Students with outstanding fees may be restricted from completing certain
administrative processes until the outstanding amount is cleared.

The university may communicate an outstanding-fee notice before applying such
restrictions.

## [SCH-5.1] Scholarship Eligibility

University scholarships are subject to the eligibility criteria specified in
the applicable scholarship announcement.

Eligibility may depend on academic performance, financial circumstances,
attendance, disciplinary status or other criteria specified for a particular
scholarship.

## [SCH-5.2] Scholarship Applications

Students must submit scholarship applications before the deadline published
for the relevant scholarship.

Incomplete applications may not be considered.

## [SCH-5.3] Scholarship Verification

The university may verify information supplied in a scholarship application.

Students may be required to provide supporting documentation where necessary.

## [SCH-5.4] Scholarship Renewal

Scholarship renewal is not automatic.

A student seeking renewal must satisfy the renewal requirements published for
the relevant scholarship programme.

## [HOST-6.1] Hostel Residence

Students residing in university accommodation must comply with hostel rules,
safety requirements and instructions issued by authorized hostel personnel.

## [HOST-6.2] Hostel Entry

The normal hostel entry time for residents is restricted after 10:00 PM.

Students arriving after the prescribed time may be required to provide a valid
reason to the hostel security staff.

## [HOST-6.3] Hostel Visitors

Visitors may enter hostel premises only during the visiting hours announced by
the hostel administration.

Visitors must comply with identification and registration requirements.

## [HOST-6.4] Hostel Rooms

Students are responsible for maintaining reasonable cleanliness and order in
their assigned rooms.

University property must not be damaged, removed or altered without
authorization.

## [HOST-6.5] Hostel Leave

Students leaving the hostel overnight must complete the prescribed leave
procedure where required by hostel administration.

## [DISC-7.1] Student Conduct

Students are expected to behave respectfully toward other students, faculty,
staff and visitors.

Conduct that materially disrupts academic or residential activities may be
subject to disciplinary review.

## [DISC-7.2] Academic Integrity

Students must complete academic work honestly.

Plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, fabrication of academic information
and other forms of academic misconduct may result in disciplinary action.

## [DISC-7.3] Disciplinary Procedure

A student accused of misconduct should receive notice of the allegation and an
opportunity to provide an explanation through the applicable disciplinary
procedure.

## [APPEAL-8.1] Academic Appeals

A student may submit an academic appeal where a university decision directly
affects the student's academic status.

Appeals must normally identify the decision being challenged and provide
relevant supporting information.

## [APPEAL-8.2] Appeal Review

Appeals are reviewed by the appropriate academic authority.

The reviewing authority may uphold, modify or refer a decision for further
consideration.

## [APPEAL-8.3] Committee Authority

The Academic Review Committee may consider exceptional academic circumstances
that are not adequately addressed by ordinary administrative procedures.

Where permitted by applicable university regulations, the committee may grant
a specific academic relaxation or waiver.

## [GRAD-9.1] Graduation Requirements

Students must satisfy the academic requirements of their degree programme
before graduation.

These requirements may include successful completion of required courses,
credits, projects, examinations and other programme requirements.

## [GRAD-9.2] Outstanding Requirements

A student who has not completed a required academic component may not normally
be awarded the degree until the requirement has been satisfied.

## [GEN-10.1] Interpretation of Regulations

University regulations should be interpreted together with applicable
departmental policies, examination instructions and formally approved
committee decisions.

Where a specific policy establishes a special procedure, that procedure may
apply to the circumstances covered by the policy.

## [GEN-10.2] Administrative Authority

Authorized university offices may issue procedural instructions necessary to
implement these regulations.

Such instructions should not be interpreted as changing substantive academic
requirements unless the issuing authority has the power to make such a
change.

## [GEN-10.3] Student Responsibility

Students are responsible for familiarizing themselves with regulations,
deadlines and procedures applicable to their programme and activities.

Failure to read a published regulation does not normally remove a student's
responsibility to comply with it.
# RuleGuard — Planted Contradictions

## [ATT-CONFLICT-1] General Attendance Requirement

Every undergraduate student must maintain a minimum attendance of 60% in each registered course to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination.

## [HOST-CONFLICT-1] Hostel Entry Time

The normal hostel entry time for residents is restricted after 11:00 PM. Students arriving after this time may be required to provide a valid reason to hostel security staff.

## [MED-CONFLICT-1] Medical Attendance Relaxation

Where a student's medical circumstances are formally verified, the Academic Review Committee may consider the student eligible for an examination with attendance as low as 60%, provided that the required medical documents have been approved.
# MediCore University Examination Policy 2026

## EXAM-14.1 — Purpose

This policy establishes the procedures and standards governing semester examinations at MediCore University. It applies to undergraduate and postgraduate students, examination coordinators, faculty members, invigilators, and administrative personnel involved in the conduct of university examinations.

The purpose of the policy is to ensure that examinations are conducted fairly, securely, consistently, and in a manner that accurately measures student learning. The policy covers examination registration, eligibility, scheduling, examination halls, permitted materials, student identification, attendance, misconduct, absence, medical circumstances, evaluation, results, revaluation, and appeals.

Students are responsible for understanding the examination requirements that apply to their registered courses. Failure to follow examination procedures may result in administrative action or disciplinary review.

## EXAM-14.2 — Examination Schedule

The University shall publish the semester examination schedule through its official academic communication channels. The schedule normally includes the examination date, start time, duration, course code, course title, and examination venue.

Students should verify the schedule before each examination period. A student who identifies a timetable conflict must notify the academic administration office as soon as possible.

Once an examination schedule has been formally published, students are expected to appear according to the published schedule unless an approved exception applies.

## EXAM-14.3 — Examination Registration

Students must complete examination registration within the registration period announced by the University.

Registration may require confirmation of course enrollment, payment of applicable examination fees, and satisfaction of academic eligibility requirements.

A student who fails to complete registration within the prescribed period may be prevented from appearing for the examination unless an authorized late-registration procedure is available.

Late registration is not automatically granted. Requests may require approval from the academic administration office.

## EXAM-14.4 — Examination Eligibility

A student may appear for a semester examination when the student has satisfied the academic requirements applicable to the course and has completed examination registration.

Attendance requirements may affect examination eligibility. The general academic attendance requirement is governed by the University's attendance regulations.

Where an approved medical or exceptional attendance provision applies, examination eligibility shall be determined after the relevant documentation and approval have been considered.

## EXAM-14.5 — Student Identification

Students must carry valid University identification when appearing for an examination.

An invigilator may request identification before allowing a student to enter the examination hall. Students unable to establish their identity may be temporarily prevented from entering while the matter is verified.

Identification documents must not be altered or misrepresented.

## EXAM-14.6 — Examination Hall Entry

Students should arrive at the examination venue before the scheduled start time.

Students arriving after the examination has begun may be admitted at the discretion of the authorized examination personnel, subject to the examination rules and security requirements.

Late arrival does not normally result in additional examination time.

A student may be refused entry where late arrival creates a significant examination-security concern or where the examination administration has closed entry.

## EXAM-14.7 — Permitted Materials

Only materials specifically authorized for a particular examination may be brought into the examination hall.

Permitted materials may include writing instruments, approved calculators, formula sheets, or other materials expressly listed in the examination instructions.

A material that is permitted in one examination is not automatically permitted in another examination.

Students must review the instructions provided for each examination before entering the examination hall.

## EXAM-14.8 — Electronic Devices

Mobile phones, smart watches, wireless earphones, tablets, and other unauthorized electronic communication devices must not be used during an examination.

Where examination instructions require electronic devices to be deposited at a designated location, students must follow those instructions.

Possession of an unauthorized electronic device may be treated as an examination-rule violation even when the student claims that the device was not actively used.

## EXAM-14.9 — Examination Conduct

Students must maintain appropriate conduct throughout the examination.

Students must not communicate with other candidates except when communication is expressly permitted by the examination instructions or an invigilator.

Students must follow reasonable instructions issued by examination personnel.

Disruptive conduct, unauthorized communication, interference with another student's work, or refusal to follow examination instructions may result in removal from the examination hall and disciplinary review.

## EXAM-14.10 — Academic Misconduct

Academic misconduct during an examination includes, but is not limited to, unauthorized communication, possession of prohibited materials, copying, impersonation, unauthorized assistance, manipulation of examination materials, or obtaining examination information through prohibited means.

Suspected misconduct should be documented by the invigilator or examination personnel.

The University shall provide the student with an opportunity to respond to allegations according to applicable disciplinary procedures.

A finding of misconduct may result in cancellation of an examination attempt, academic penalties, or further disciplinary action.

## EXAM-14.11 — Examination Paper Security

Examination papers and other confidential examination materials must be handled according to University security procedures.

Students must not photograph, copy, distribute, or otherwise reproduce examination papers without authorization.

Examination personnel must take reasonable measures to prevent unauthorized disclosure of examination materials before and during examinations.

## EXAM-14.12 — Answer Sheet Requirements

Students must use the answer sheets or examination systems specified for the examination.

Where required, students must write their registration number, course information, and other identifying information in the designated fields.

Students must not intentionally include identifying information in locations where anonymous evaluation is required.

Answer sheets must be submitted according to the instructions provided by examination personnel.

## EXAM-14.13 — Absence From Examination

A student who does not attend a scheduled examination without an approved reason may be recorded as absent.

Absence does not automatically create a right to a supplementary examination.

Students who miss an examination because of circumstances recognized under University policy may submit a formal request for consideration.

Requests should normally be submitted promptly and supported by appropriate documentation.

## EXAM-14.14 — Medical Examination Absence

A student unable to attend an examination because of a significant medical circumstance may request academic consideration.

The request should normally include documentation from a recognized medical professional or institution.

The University may verify submitted documentation where necessary.

Approval of a medical request does not guarantee a particular examination outcome. The academic administration office shall determine the appropriate academic arrangement according to applicable procedures.

## EXAM-14.15 — Emergency Circumstances

The University may consider examination requests involving serious and unexpected circumstances such as hospitalization, major accidents, or other verified emergencies.

Routine inconvenience, travel difficulties, personal scheduling conflicts, or failure to check the published examination schedule normally do not constitute sufficient grounds for special examination arrangements.

The decision shall consider the evidence provided and the academic impact of the circumstance.

## EXAM-14.16 — Examination Duration

The examination duration shall be specified in the examination instructions.

Students must stop writing or submitting responses when the examination period ends.

Students who continue working after the official end time may be subject to an examination-rule violation.

Invigilators shall provide reasonable warnings regarding the approaching end of the examination where operationally feasible.

## EXAM-14.17 — Leaving the Examination Hall

Students normally should remain in the examination hall until the minimum departure period specified by examination personnel has elapsed.

A student requiring an emergency departure should inform an invigilator.

Students must submit examination materials before leaving where required.

A student who leaves the examination hall may not normally return unless specifically authorized.

## EXAM-14.18 — Evaluation of Examinations

Examination responses shall be evaluated according to the approved assessment scheme for the relevant course.

Faculty members and authorized evaluators shall apply academic assessment criteria consistently.

Evaluation should be based on the student's submitted work and the approved marking requirements.

The University may conduct moderation or quality checks where required.

## EXAM-14.19 — Examination Results

Examination results shall be published through authorized University systems.

Students are responsible for reviewing their results and reporting apparent administrative errors within the applicable review period.

Publication of results does not prevent correction of verified administrative or calculation errors.

## EXAM-14.20 — Revaluation and Review

A student who believes that an examination result requires formal review may submit a revaluation or review request when the applicable process is available.

The request must be submitted within the announced period and may require payment of an administrative fee.

Revaluation shall be conducted according to the University's approved procedure.

A revaluation may result in the original marks being confirmed, increased, or changed according to the applicable rules.

## EXAM-14.21 — Result Correction

Administrative errors identified after result publication may be corrected following verification.

Examples include calculation errors, data-entry errors, incorrect course mapping, or other demonstrable administrative mistakes.

The University shall maintain an appropriate record of verified corrections.

## EXAM-14.22 — Supplementary Examination

Where University regulations provide for supplementary examinations, eligibility shall be determined according to the applicable academic rules.

A supplementary examination is not automatically available to every student who fails or misses an examination.

The University shall publish eligibility conditions, registration requirements, fees, and examination schedules where supplementary examinations are offered.

## EXAM-14.23 — Examination Appeals

Students may submit an academic appeal when they believe that an examination decision has been made incorrectly or that an approved procedure was not followed.

Appeals must identify the decision being challenged and provide relevant supporting information.

An appeal should be submitted within the prescribed period.

The appeal process does not guarantee a change in academic results.

## EXAM-14.24 — Examination Committee

The Examination Committee may review examination-related matters requiring institutional consideration.

The committee may consider cases involving examination misconduct, special circumstances, procedural disputes, examination administration, and other matters referred to it.

The committee may request additional information from students, faculty members, invigilators, or administrative offices.

## EXAM-14.25 — Confidentiality

Examination records, student submissions, misconduct reports, and review decisions should be handled confidentially and accessed only by authorized personnel.

Information may be shared when required for legitimate academic administration, disciplinary proceedings, legal obligations, or quality assurance.

## EXAM-14.26 — Accessibility Arrangements

Students requiring approved accessibility arrangements should contact the appropriate University office before the examination period whenever reasonably possible.

Approved arrangements may include additional time, accessible examination facilities, assistive technology, or other reasonable measures.

Accessibility arrangements must be formally approved and communicated to examination personnel.

## EXAM-14.27 — Technical Failure During Digital Examination

Where an examination is conducted digitally, students must report technical problems promptly through the designated examination support channel.

The University may verify technical records, submission logs, or system information when assessing a technical incident.

Where a verified technical failure materially affects an examination, the University may provide an appropriate remedy according to examination procedures.

## EXAM-14.28 — Examination Records

The University shall maintain examination records including registration information, attendance records, submitted results, approved review requests, and other records required for academic administration.

Records shall be retained according to applicable University record-management requirements.

## EXAM-14.29 — Student Responsibility

Students are responsible for checking examination schedules, completing registration, carrying required identification, following examination instructions, and complying with academic integrity requirements.

Failure to understand a published requirement does not normally exempt a student from complying with it.

Students should seek clarification from the appropriate academic office when a requirement is unclear.

## EXAM-14.30 — Interpretation

Questions regarding interpretation of this examination policy shall be referred to the authorized academic administration office.

Where another University regulation contains a more specific requirement, the more specific provision may apply to the relevant situation.

The University may review and amend examination procedures when necessary to improve academic administration, security, accessibility, or fairness.

**End of Examination Policy**

# MediCore University Fee and Financial Policy 2026

## [FEE-11.1] Fee Schedule

All students enrolled in an academic programme are required to pay the applicable
tuition and institutional fees for each semester.

The university publishes the fee schedule before the beginning of the relevant
payment period.

The fee schedule shall identify the amount payable, payment period and standard
payment deadline.

Students are responsible for checking the official fee schedule and ensuring
that payments are completed within the applicable period.

## [FEE-11.2] Standard Payment Deadline

The standard deadline for semester fee payment shall be the date published in
the official fee schedule.

Unless a separate approved arrangement applies, students are expected to
complete payment by the published deadline.

A payment made after the standard deadline may result in an additional late
payment charge.

## [FEE-11.3] Late Payment Period

The university may establish a late-payment period following the standard
payment deadline.

Where a late-payment period is officially announced, students may complete
their payment during that period subject to the applicable late-payment charge.

The existence of a late-payment period does not create a permanent right to
pay fees after the standard deadline.

## [FEE-11.4] Administrative Restrictions

A student with outstanding fees may be restricted from completing specified
administrative activities.

Such activities may include examination registration, receipt of official
documents or other processes identified by the university.

Restrictions should be communicated to affected students through an official
communication channel.

## [FEE-11.5] Emergency Financial Circumstances

Students experiencing documented financial hardship may submit a request for
additional time to pay their semester fees.

The request must be submitted before the standard payment deadline wherever
reasonably possible.

Submission of a request does not by itself extend the payment deadline.

## [FEE-11.6] Payment Extension

An approved payment extension may allow a student to complete payment after the
standard deadline without being treated as an ordinary late payment.

The extension must be formally approved by an authorized financial officer or
committee.

The approval should specify the final date by which payment must be completed.

## [FEE-11.7] Fee Refunds

Refund requests must be submitted according to the applicable refund schedule.

The amount refunded, if any, may depend on the date of withdrawal and the
reason for withdrawal.

Administrative charges may be deducted where permitted by the applicable
refund policy.

## [FEE-11.8] Refund Processing

Approved refunds are normally processed through the payment method or bank
details registered with the university.

Students may be asked to verify their payment information before a refund is
processed.

## [FEE-11.9] Financial Assistance

Students may apply for financial assistance programmes announced by the
university.

Financial assistance may be subject to academic, financial and administrative
eligibility criteria.

Receiving financial assistance does not automatically remove the student's
responsibility to satisfy applicable fee requirements.

## [FEE-11.10] Fee Disputes

A student who believes that an amount has been incorrectly charged may submit a
fee dispute to the finance office.

The dispute should include the student's identification details, the disputed
amount and supporting documentation.

## [FEE-11.11] Fee Dispute During Registration

A pending fee dispute does not automatically prevent the university from
applying ordinary registration deadlines.

Students should contact the finance office promptly when a disputed amount
could affect registration.

## [FEE-11.12] Committee Review of Financial Cases

Exceptional financial cases may be referred to the Financial Review Committee.

The committee may consider documented circumstances and may recommend an
extension, installment arrangement or other permitted relief.

## [FEE-11.13] Installment Arrangements

Where permitted, students may request payment through an approved installment
arrangement.

An installment arrangement must identify the number of installments and the
date on which each installment becomes due.

Failure to comply with an approved installment arrangement may result in
withdrawal of the arrangement.

## [FEE-11.14] Payment Confirmation

Students should retain electronic or physical evidence of completed payments
until the payment has been reflected in the university's financial system.

A transaction receipt alone does not guarantee that a payment has been
successfully credited if the transaction is subsequently reversed.

## [FEE-11.15] Communication of Deadlines

Fee deadlines may be communicated through the student portal, official email,
published notices or other officially designated channels.

Students are expected to monitor these channels during the payment period.

## [FEE-11.16] Exceptional Deadline Provision

In exceptional circumstances, the Finance Office may authorize a student to
complete payment up to **20 August** even when the standard semester fee
deadline has passed.

Such approval requires a documented reason and confirmation from the
authorized officer.

## [FEE-11.17] Standard Academic Deadline

For the 2026 academic session, semester fees must ordinarily be paid no later
than **15 August**.

Payments completed after this date are considered late unless an approved
exception or extension applies.

## [FEE-11.18] Relationship With Other Policies

This policy should be read together with the academic regulations,
scholarship policy and other financial instructions issued by the university.

Where a specific financial provision applies to a particular category of
student, that provision may govern the circumstances covered by it.
# MediCore University Hostel Policy 2026

## [HOST-12.1] Purpose of Hostel Regulations

The university hostel provides residential accommodation for eligible students
and aims to maintain a safe, orderly and supportive living environment.

All residents must comply with hostel regulations, safety procedures and
reasonable instructions issued by authorized hostel personnel.

## [HOST-12.2] Eligibility for Hostel Accommodation

Hostel accommodation may be provided to students who satisfy the eligibility
criteria published by the university.

Allocation may depend on availability, programme requirements, distance from
the university, student category and other criteria established by the hostel
administration.

A hostel room is allocated to a specific student and may not ordinarily be
transferred to another person without authorization.

## [HOST-12.3] Room Allocation

The hostel administration determines room allocation.

Students may submit requests for room changes where a genuine academic,
medical, safety or administrative reason exists.

A request for a room change does not guarantee that another room will be
available.

## [HOST-12.4] Normal Hostel Curfew

Residents are expected to return to the hostel by **10:00 PM** on ordinary
academic days.

After 10:00 PM, entry may be restricted and residents arriving after the
curfew may be asked to provide a reason for their late arrival.

Repeated violations may be referred to the hostel administration.

## [HOST-12.5] Late Entry Permission

A student who expects to arrive after the normal curfew may request permission
for late entry through the hostel administration.

Permission should ordinarily be requested before the student leaves the
campus or residence area.

In emergencies, permission may be requested after the student has arrived.

## [HOST-12.6] Academic Activities After Curfew

Students participating in officially authorized university activities may be
permitted to return after the normal hostel curfew.

The activity should be organized or recognized by an authorized university
department, faculty member or student affairs office.

Students should carry evidence of participation when requested by hostel
security.

## [HOST-12.7] Hostel Security

Security personnel may verify the identity of residents entering hostel
premises.

Students must cooperate with reasonable security checks.

Security personnel should maintain records of unusual or exceptional late
entries where required for safety purposes.

## [HOST-12.8] Visitor Policy

Visitors may enter hostel premises only during approved visiting hours.

Visitors must register at the designated security point.

Residents are responsible for the conduct of their visitors while they are on
hostel premises.

## [HOST-12.9] Overnight Visitors

Visitors may not ordinarily stay overnight in student accommodation.

An exception may be considered where written permission has been granted by
the hostel administration.

Unauthorized overnight stays may be treated as a hostel rule violation.

## [HOST-12.10] Room Cleanliness

Residents must maintain reasonable cleanliness in their rooms.

Food waste, packaging and other waste should be disposed of using designated
waste facilities.

Students may be required to clean areas affected by activities originating
from their room.

## [HOST-12.11] Hostel Property

Furniture, electrical equipment and other hostel property must not be removed
from assigned rooms or common areas without authorization.

Students may be held responsible for damage caused by intentional misuse or
negligence.

## [HOST-12.12] Electrical Safety

Students must not use electrical equipment that creates an unreasonable fire
or electrical hazard.

High-power appliances may be restricted in accordance with hostel safety
instructions.

Students should report damaged electrical outlets, exposed wiring or other
hazards immediately.

## [HOST-12.13] Prohibited Activities

Residents must not engage in activities that create a significant safety
risk, disturb other residents or damage university property.

The hostel administration may issue additional reasonable safety instructions
where circumstances require them.

## [HOST-12.14] Quiet Hours

Quiet hours normally begin at **10:30 PM** and continue until **6:30 AM**.

During quiet hours, residents should avoid loud music, shouting and other
unnecessary noise.

Academic discussion conducted at a reasonable volume is permitted unless it
disturbs other residents.

## [HOST-12.15] Hostel Leave

Students intending to remain away from the hostel overnight should complete
the applicable hostel leave procedure.

The procedure may require the student to provide the destination, expected
return date and an emergency contact.

## [HOST-12.16] Emergency Leave

In an emergency, a student may leave the hostel before completing the normal
leave procedure.

The student should inform the hostel administration as soon as reasonably
possible.

## [HOST-12.17] Weekend Travel

Students may travel outside the university campus during weekends provided
that their academic and hostel responsibilities are not affected.

Students remaining away overnight should follow the applicable leave
procedure.

## [HOST-12.18] Curfew Exception for Registered Activities

For the purpose of this policy, a student participating in a **registered
university activity may return to the hostel until 11:00 PM** without obtaining
individual late-entry permission.

The activity must be listed or approved by the relevant university authority.

The student may be required to show the activity schedule or other reasonable
evidence of participation.

## [HOST-12.19] Ordinary Curfew

Except where an approved exception applies, students must return to the hostel
by **10:00 PM**.

A student who has not received an applicable exception and arrives after
10:00 PM may be subject to the normal late-entry procedure.

## [HOST-12.20] Curfew and Academic Responsibility

Permission to return after curfew does not excuse a student from attending
classes, completing assignments or following other academic requirements.

Students remain responsible for managing their schedules appropriately.

## [HOST-12.21] Health and Safety Exceptions

A student facing an immediate health or safety concern should seek appropriate
assistance rather than attempting to comply with ordinary hostel timing
requirements.

Emergency circumstances should be reported to hostel administration as soon
as reasonably possible.

## [HOST-12.22] Disciplinary Review

Repeated or serious hostel violations may be referred to the appropriate
disciplinary authority.

The student should ordinarily be informed of the allegation and given an
opportunity to provide an explanation.

## [HOST-12.23] Hostel Complaints

Residents may submit complaints concerning accommodation, security, cleanliness
or other hostel matters through the designated hostel administration channel.

Complaints should contain sufficient information for the administration to
investigate the matter.

## [HOST-12.24] Interpretation

Hostel regulations should be interpreted together with university safety
policies and authorized instructions issued by the student affairs office.

Where an approved exception specifically applies to a student's circumstances,
the exception should be considered together with the ordinary hostel rule.

## [HOST-12.25] Responsibility of Residents

Every resident is responsible for becoming familiar with the hostel rules.

Failure to read a published hostel regulation does not normally exempt a
resident from compliance.

## [HOST-12.26] Review of Hostel Rules

The university may periodically review hostel regulations to reflect changes
in accommodation arrangements, safety requirements or student needs.

Changes should be communicated through an officially designated channel.
# MediCore University Scholarship and Financial Assistance Policy 2026

## [SCH-13.1] Purpose

The university may provide scholarships and financial assistance to eligible
students to support academic participation and reduce financial barriers.

Scholarships may be funded by the university, external organizations,
alumni, charitable foundations or other approved sources.

Each scholarship programme may have its own eligibility requirements and
application procedure.

## [SCH-13.2] Scholarship Categories

Scholarships may include merit-based scholarships, need-based assistance,
achievement awards, research scholarships, sports scholarships and other
categories approved by the university.

A student may apply only for scholarships for which the student satisfies the
published eligibility requirements.

## [SCH-13.3] Merit Scholarship

A merit scholarship may be awarded to students who achieve the academic
performance specified in the relevant scholarship announcement.

Academic performance may be evaluated using semester grades, cumulative
academic performance or another officially specified measure.

## [SCH-13.4] Financial Assistance

Need-based financial assistance may be provided to students experiencing
documented financial difficulties.

Applicants may be required to provide information concerning household
income, educational expenses and other relevant financial circumstances.

The university may verify information supplied by an applicant.

## [SCH-13.5] Scholarship Application

Students must submit scholarship applications using the procedure specified in
the applicable scholarship announcement.

Applications submitted after the published deadline may normally be rejected.

## [SCH-13.6] Required Documents

A scholarship application may require academic records, identification,
income documentation, bank information or other supporting material.

The required documents shall be identified in the relevant scholarship
announcement.

Students are responsible for ensuring that submitted documents are accurate
and complete.

## [SCH-13.7] Incomplete Applications

The scholarship office may contact an applicant when a required document is
missing or unclear.

The applicant may be given an opportunity to provide the missing information
within the period specified by the scholarship office.

An incomplete application may be rejected where the applicant fails to provide
the requested information within the applicable period.

## [SCH-13.8] Scholarship Selection

Scholarship decisions may consider academic performance, financial
circumstances, extracurricular achievement, leadership, community
participation and other published criteria.

The selection process should be applied consistently to applicants within the
same scholarship category.

## [SCH-13.9] Scholarship Committee

A Scholarship Committee may review eligible applications and recommend
recipients.

The committee may request clarification from applicants where necessary.

The committee's decision shall be recorded through the applicable university
procedure.

## [SCH-13.10] Scholarship Award

A scholarship award shall specify the amount or benefit provided and the
period for which the award applies.

An award for one semester does not automatically establish entitlement to the
same award in subsequent semesters.

## [SCH-13.11] Scholarship Renewal

Renewal may depend on continued academic performance, attendance, disciplinary
standing and any additional criteria published for the scholarship.

Students must complete any required renewal process before the specified
deadline.

## [SCH-13.12] Attendance and Scholarships

Where attendance is listed as an eligibility requirement, the scholarship
office may use official attendance records supplied by the academic
administration.

Attendance requirements for scholarships are separate from general
examination eligibility unless the applicable scholarship rules expressly
state otherwise.

## [SCH-13.13] Scholarship Suspension

A scholarship may be suspended where a student fails to satisfy continuing
eligibility requirements.

The student should ordinarily be informed of the reason for suspension.

## [SCH-13.14] Scholarship Cancellation

A scholarship may be cancelled if it is established that the student
knowingly supplied false information or failed to meet a mandatory eligibility
condition.

Cancellation decisions should follow the applicable review procedure.

## [SCH-13.15] Change in Financial Circumstances

Students receiving need-based assistance should notify the scholarship office
if a material change occurs in the circumstances on which the award was based.

The university may review the continued eligibility of the student.

## [SCH-13.16] Multiple Scholarships

A student may not automatically combine multiple university-funded
scholarships.

Where a scholarship announcement contains restrictions on combining awards,
those restrictions apply to the relevant scholarship.

Students should disclose other scholarships when requested.

## [SCH-13.17] External Scholarships

Students may apply for scholarships provided by external organizations.

External scholarships are governed by the rules of the organization providing
the award.

The university may require students to notify the scholarship office when an
external scholarship affects university financial assistance.

## [SCH-13.18] Scholarship Payment

Scholarship benefits may be credited toward tuition fees, deposited into a
registered student account or paid through another officially approved
mechanism.

The payment method depends on the scholarship programme.

## [SCH-13.19] Scholarship Appeals

An applicant who believes that a scholarship decision was made incorrectly
may submit an appeal within the period specified by the scholarship office.

An appeal should identify the decision being challenged and provide relevant
supporting information.

## [SCH-13.20] Appeal Review

Scholarship appeals may be reviewed by an authority separate from the initial
application reviewer where required by university procedure.

The reviewing authority may uphold the original decision, modify it where
authorized or refer the matter for further review.

## [SCH-13.21] Academic Misconduct

A student found responsible for serious academic misconduct may become
ineligible for certain scholarship programmes.

The consequences depend on the requirements of the relevant scholarship.

## [SCH-13.22] Disciplinary Status

Scholarship eligibility may be affected by disciplinary action where the
relevant scholarship rules identify disciplinary standing as an eligibility
condition.

A pending allegation does not automatically establish that a student has
violated a disciplinary requirement.

## [SCH-13.23] Scholarship Records

Scholarship applications and decisions should be maintained according to
university record-management requirements.

Access to financial information should be restricted to authorized personnel.

## [SCH-13.24] Privacy

Information supplied for financial assistance should be used only for
legitimate scholarship administration, verification and related university
purposes.

The university should take reasonable measures to prevent unauthorized
disclosure.

## [SCH-13.25] Scholarship Communication

Scholarship deadlines, eligibility requirements and application instructions
may be communicated through the student portal, official email or other
designated university channels.

Students are responsible for checking official communication concerning
scholarships.

## [SCH-13.26] Exceptional Scholarship Cases

Exceptional scholarship cases may be referred to the Scholarship Committee
when circumstances are not adequately addressed by the ordinary scholarship
procedure.

The committee may recommend an appropriate solution within its authority.

## [SCH-13.27] Scholarship Funding

Scholarship awards are subject to the availability of funds allocated to the
relevant scholarship programme.

The publication of a scholarship opportunity does not guarantee that every
eligible applicant will receive an award.

## [SCH-13.28] End of Scholarship

A scholarship normally ends when the award period expires, the student no
longer satisfies the eligibility requirements or the student's programme
status changes in a way that makes the award inapplicable.

The scholarship office may communicate the end of an award to the student.

## [SCH-13.29] Student Responsibility

Students are responsible for reading the scholarship conditions applicable to
their award.

Students should promptly communicate material changes that could affect their
eligibility.

## [SCH-13.30] Interpretation

Where a scholarship-specific rule differs from a general financial assistance
rule, the scholarship-specific provision should be considered for students
covered by that programme.

Questions concerning interpretation may be referred to the Scholarship Office.

MediCore University Student Services Policy 2026
STU-15.1 — Student Support Services
MediCore University provides academic and administrative support services intended to help students
successfully participate in university life. Student services may include academic advising, career guidance,
library assistance, accessibility support, financial guidance, and general administrative assistance.
STU-15.2 — Academic Advising
Students may consult their academic advisor regarding course selection, academic progression, examination
requirements, attendance concerns, graduation planning, and other academic matters. Students remain
responsible for verifying their own registration and academic records.
STU-15.3 — Student Records
Students may request access to academic records through the designated University procedure. Requests
must contain sufficient information for the University to identify the relevant student record. Corrections to
records may be requested when a student identifies a possible administrative error.
STU-15.4 — Identity Verification
Certain student services may require identity verification before information is disclosed or an administrative
request is processed. University personnel should use reasonable procedures to protect student information
from unauthorized access.
STU-15.5 — Library Services
Students with valid University enrollment may use library facilities subject to library rules. Borrowed materials
must be returned within the applicable borrowing period. Students may be responsible for replacement costs
or other charges arising from lost or seriously damaged materials.
STU-15.6 — Career Services
The Career Services Office may provide assistance with career planning, resume preparation, interview
preparation, employer events, internships, and placement-related activities. Participation in a career service
does not guarantee employment or placement.
STU-15.7 — Student Complaints
Students may submit complaints regarding academic administration, facilities, student services, or other
University matters through the designated complaint procedure. Complaints should contain sufficient
information to allow the University to understand and investigate the issue.

STU-15.8 — Complaint Review
The receiving office may request additional information before reviewing a complaint. Where a complaint
concerns another University office, the matter may be forwarded to an appropriate administrative authority.
STU-15.9 — Accessibility Support
Students who require approved accessibility support may contact the designated University office. Support
arrangements should be based on documented requirements and reasonable institutional procedures.
STU-15.10 — Emergency Student Assistance
Students experiencing an urgent administrative or academic difficulty should contact the appropriate
University office as soon as reasonably possible. Emergency assistance is subject to verification and
availability of appropriate University resources.
STU-15.11 — Communication
Official student-service communications may be delivered through University email, student portals, notices,
or other authorized channels. Students are responsible for checking official communications relevant to their
academic and administrative responsibilities.
STU-15.12 — Service Requests
Student-service requests should be submitted using the procedure specified by the responsible office.
Requests submitted through unofficial channels may not be processed until they are submitted through the
appropriate system.
STU-15.13 — Processing Times
Processing times vary depending on the type and complexity of a request. A standard processing period does
not guarantee completion by a particular date when additional verification or information is required.
STU-15.14 — Privacy
Student-service personnel should handle personal and academic information responsibly. Information should
be accessed or disclosed only when required for legitimate University functions or when otherwise authorized.
STU-15.15 — Service Eligibility
Eligibility for a particular student service may depend on enrollment status, academic status, documentation,
deadlines, or other requirements established by the responsible University office.
STU-15.16 — Appeals

Where a student-service decision includes an appeal mechanism, the student may submit an appeal
according to the applicable procedure. Appeals should identify the decision being challenged and provide
relevant supporting information.
STU-15.17 — Interpretation
Questions regarding interpretation of this policy should be directed to the responsible student-services
authority. More specific University regulations may take precedence where they directly govern a particular
student-service matter.
